subject: Performance SLO / context window discussion - follow up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — latency & context-window follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really helpful to see FinCo's live demo and your latency constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call:

- Target latency: sub-400ms p95 for single-turn customer prompts (avg token output ~120 tokens).
- Throughput & concurrency: plan for sustained 250 QPS with spike capacity to 500 concurrent requests during peak reconciliation runs.
- Streaming: must support token-by-token streaming for UI responsiveness; clients expect first-token within ~80ms.
- Context window: many of your queries include ~10–15 documents per request (~6k tokens input); you also expect up to 2k tokens of model-generated output.
- Impact note: based on the context lengths, we flagged that max context > 8k tokens will increase compute and could push p95 beyond target on default model variants without batching/quantization adjustments.

Attachments: I'm sharing our SLO reference doc and an example of service-level logs (attached) that show how we measure p50/p95 and token accounting.

Next steps:
1) We'll validate streaming-first-token numbers against your sample requests — can you send a small set of representative payloads? (Priya, we discussed anonymized logs.)
2) Logan will sketch a config: batching windows, KV cache hints, and a recommended model/quant profile for the 8k+ context case.
3) Tentative architecture call next week to align on dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback.

I'll follow up with the config sketch and a short perf spreadsheet by EOD.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>

Date: 2027-04-28T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — latency & context-window follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary.

A few clarifying Qs from our side:
1) When you say "first-token within ~80ms", is that measured from HTTP/TCP accept or from last-byte of the input? Our client measures from send-complete.
2) For the context window — we currently concatenate ~10 documents, average 600 tokens each, so closer to 6k input tokens. You mentioned 8k+ as a threshold — is that a hard cutoff for increased latency or a sliding cost curve?
3) Any immediate guidance on whether we should truncate inputs server-side, or rely on Redwood's prefix-KV caching + smarter retrieval to avoid re-sending full context each request?

We'll prepare anonymized sample payloads (Priya will drop them in the Drive link).

— Alex
Head of AI, FinCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — latency & context-window follow-up

Great questions — answers inline below.

Alex — short answers first:
1) Our first-token metric is measured from request accept (server receive) to first token emitted. If your client measures from send-complete, add typical client-to-server network time; we'll align measurements in the perf call.
2) 8k tokens isn't a hard cutoff — it's where typical autoregressive memory + KV cache management and kernel selection start increasing per-token compute significantly on standard FP16 model variants. Latency increases smoothly with context size, but you'll see a step change when crossing certain implementation thresholds (e.g., attention kernel switching and memory I/O patterns). We'll include a plot in the perf spreadsheet.
3) Short-term: smart truncation helps, but it's better to rely on retrieval + prefix-KV caching to avoid re-transmitting large repeated context every request. If you have many repeated documents per user, caching can reduce p95 by 20–40% depending on hit rate.

Logan is putting together quantified recommendations (batching window, concurrency targets, suggested quantization) — see draft attachment. Key trade-offs:
- Smaller batching windows reduce tail latency but lower throughput efficiency.
- INT8 quant can reduce compute latency/cost but may slightly affect token generation consistency — we'll propose specific model variants for FinCo's tolerance.
- Streaming-first-token: on dedicated infra we can consistently hit <80ms for typical 2–3k input+100 token output; at 6k+ inputs we expect first-token to increase and p95 to drift towards the 300–500ms range unless caching/batching optimizations applied.

Next immediate asks from us:
- Please upload 10 representative requests to the Drive folder (anonymized). Priya, once we have these we'll run an instrumented pass and share per-request traces.
- Logan: can you confirm whether Dedicated capacity quote should include a KV cache layer and estimated lifecycle cost?

I'll schedule the architecture call and drop the perf spreadsheet link in the thread.

Thanks,
Marissa
